items.title: Miti seeks Budget 2027 allocations to accelerate semiconductor industry, expand Malaysian exports
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 5 — The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) has submitted 11 initiatives to the Finance Ministry (MOF) for consideration in Budget 2027, which will be tabled next month. Deputy Miti Minister Sim Tze Tzin said priority would be given to efforts to accelerate the semiconductor industry as a high-growth, high-value sector capable of creating more jobs for Malaysians. Sim, who is also Bayan Baru member of parliament, said Miti had also proposed allocations to help Malaysian companies, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises, penetrate new and previously underexplored overseas markets.

items.title: The haze demands more than another Asean pledge
items.summary: The city is completely smothered in a mood-depressing smog as forest fires raged uncontrollably in much of Indonesia's Kalimantan, producing the toxic haze that spread across the border into Sarawak. Indonesia accepted Malaysia's offer, even though Wan Junaidi acknowledged the particular difficulty of accessing the remote interior of Borneo where fires raged. Wan Junaidi also suggests the pooling of resources within Asean.

items.title: Puspakom eyes 24-hour operations from January
items.summary: KLANG: The Computerised Vehicle Inspection Centre (Puspakom) plans to operate 24 hours a day from next January to provide greater convenience to the public for vehicle inspections. Puspakom chief executive officer Mahmood Razak Bahman said the plan would depend on public response to the extension of operating hours to seven days a week from November, as well as the availability of sufficient manpower. Meanwhile, Mahmood said Puspakom was introducing several other initiatives, including a new "community hero" recognition award and expanded on-site inspection services for customers.

items.title: Two more survivors, including Chinese national, rescued 10 days after devastating Nepal floods
items.summary: KATHMANDU: A Chinese national was pulled alive from a tunnel in Nepal on Saturday, authorities said, 10 days after a wall of ice, rock and mud tore through a Himalayan valley, killing more than 1,300 people. The Nepali army said Lu Haitao was rescued from inside a 225-metre tunnel at the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project. On Friday, rescue workers pulled two people from another tunnel at the Upper Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station on the same river.

items.title: Sarawak haze crisis prompts nationwide plea to stop open burning, shield schools and businesses
items.summary: SARIKEI, Sept 5 — All parties are urged to refrain from open burning activities to prevent the haze situation in Sarawak from worsening and posing risks to public health and daily activities. Special Select Committee on Infrastructure, Transportation and Communication chairman Datuk Yusuf Abd Wahab said all open burning activities, including the disposal of rubbish and clearing of forests through fire, must cease until the situation returns to normal. Put these activities on hold until the haze situation improves.

items.title: Ops Vulture arrests two in Teluk Intan, police seize five ATM cards, gold jewellery
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 5 — Police arrested two men yesterday over unlicensed money-lending and possession of ATM cards belonging to others, during an operation codenamed Ops Vulture in Teluk Intan. Hilir Perak police chief ACP Chua Kok Lian said the suspects were arrested by the district’s Commercial Crime Investigation Division. Two ATM cards belonging to other people and RM300 cash were found on him.

items.title: Iraqis queue for fuel as regional war disrupts imports
items.summary: BAGHDAD: Drivers formed long lines outside fuel stations in Baghdad on Saturday as gasoline supplies dropped in oil-rich Iraq due to import disruptions caused by the Middle East war. Despite being OPEC's second largest oil producer, Iraq imports oil derivatives because its refineries do not produce enough gasoline to meet domestic demand. "It is unreasonable that we produce so many barrels of oil a day, yet still do not have enough gasoline to meet our daily needs," Hashem told AFP outside a fuel station in central Baghdad.

items.title: Teo Nie Ching says Meta must extend Facebook, Instagram safeguards worldwide for under‑18s
items.summary: Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the safety features should not be limited to users in the United States, as young people in other countries, including Malaysia, also face the risk of internet addiction. She said the measures are in line with the government’s direction to ensure that young people, particularly those under 16, do not use social media excessively. Teo said measures to protect young people must be implemented comprehensively by all social media platforms and not just Meta.

items.title: Philippine VP Duterte posts bail over 'grave threats' against president
items.summary: MANILA: Philippine vice president Sara Duterte posted bail at a Manila courthouse on Saturday, a day after an arrest warrant was issued over her alleged death threat against the country's president. She later said the comments had been misconstrued. she said.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin: Cancer screening must reach every Malaysian
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah has called for greater emphasis on early cancer detection, stressing that access to health screening should be available to all Malaysians regardless of their social or economic background. In his address at the launch of the National Cancer Congress Malaysia 2026 today, the ruler said a national screening programme should reach everyone, describing it as an important investment in the nation's wellbeing. On the congress, Sultan Nazrin outlined three priorities, calling for stronger research, evidence-based policymaking and greater public awareness of cancer.

items.title: Budget 2027 plan: Fadhlina pushes Kasih Madani training expansion to protect children nationwide
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 5 — Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek will propose including the Kasih Madani home childminder training programme in Budget 2027 to provide greater childcare and safety support for working mothers. Fadhlina, who is also the Nibong Tebal MP, said expanding the initiative would allow more childminders to receive formal training, improve childcare quality, and strengthen the home childcare ecosystem. Sharing her personal experience, Fadhlina revealed that three of her children were cared for by home childminders, and her second child was subjected to physical abuse by a childminder.

items.title: NKVE collapse: RSEA wants safety audit of highway structures
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Road Safety Expert Association (RSEA) has called for an immediate structural safety audit of potentially hazardous structures along Malaysia's major expressways following the collapse of a large structure onto the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) near Shah Alam last night. RSEA founder and road safety and motorsports adviser Jamil Manan Supri said the incident raised a critical road safety issue, stressing that structures located beside or above high-speed traffic must remain structurally sound throughout their service life. "RSEA therefore calls for an immediate structural safety audit of all large billboards, advertising structures, gantries and other potentially hazardous structures located along major expressways, with priority given to those positioned above, immediately beside or within the potential fall zone of live traffic," he said in a statement.

items.title: Sarawak remains worst hit as six areas record very unhealthy air quality
items.summary: Data published on the Department of Environment's Facebook page showed that 25 of 68 monitoring stations nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality, while another six recorded very unhealthy readings. Stations recording unhealthy air quality included ILP Miri (191), Mukah (190), Miri (184), Sarikei (180), Sibu (176), Kimanis (171) and Labuan (170). The data also showed that 26 stations recorded moderate air quality, while 10 recorded good air quality.

items.title: Emergency remains: Uggah says Serian still under haze alert despite API improvement
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 5 — Serian remains under the haze emergency despite its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading improving from the hazardous level, with the Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) continuing to closely monitor the situation. SDMC chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said in a statement today that the Serian air quality monitoring station recorded an API reading of 334 as at 10am, placing the area in the hazardous category. Uggah said the monitoring would be carried out before any recommendation was made to the Sarawak Premier and Prime Minister regarding the status of the emergency in Serian.

items.title: Immigration steps up hunt for foreigners issued fraudulent PLKS
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Immigration Department will intensify enforcement operations to track down foreigners holding more than 1,300 Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) believed to have been irregularly approved through a syndicate uncovered under Op Crack. Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department's enforcement division was also gathering intelligence on the ground to identify and locate foreigners holding the improperly approved passes. Zakaria said the department also welcomed information from the public that could assist enforcement officers in locating foreigners holding the irregularly approved PLKS.

items.title: Indonesia rescues second orangutan mother and baby from wildfire
items.summary: JAKARTA: An orangutan mother and her baby, threatened by encroaching wildfires to their habitat in Indonesia, were rescued earlier this week, authorities said in a statement Saturday. The orangutan pair had been under observation since July after being spotted in a plantation area near a forest in West Kalimantan, a local natural resources conservation agency said in a statement. "Exposure to smoke over a period of time... can affect the orangutan's respiratory system, especially when smoke concentrations in the habitat are very high," YIARI's veterinarian Komara, who like many Indonesians uses only one name, said in a statement.

items.title: Air we breathe could be harming children, says Sultan Nazrin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Chemical emissions from industries, vehicle exhaust fumes, as well as water and soil pollution can no longer be regarded solely as environmental issues, as prolonged exposure has been linked to various cancers, including among children. Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah said cancer prevention efforts should not focus solely on factors such as smoking and diet, but also address chemicals released by factories, vehicle emissions and other pollutants children may inhale or be exposed to daily. Sultan Nazrin said this at the launch of the National Cancer Congress Malaysia 2026 and the coffee table book, A Breath For The Future: Malaysia's National Lung Health Initiative.

items.title: Orange suits out, double standards must too, says criminologist
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission's (MACC) decision to stop requiring suspects to wear its orange uniform during remand proceedings is appropriate, but the policy must be applied equally regardless of a person's status, wealth or political position, said a criminologist. When someone is brought to court for remand, that person is still a suspect. Haezreena said allowing suspects to appear in civilian clothing could also reinforce the presumption of innocence, particularly given the strong visual association between the orange uniform and criminality.

items.title: Hadi claims Pas leaders were offered foreign help to topple government
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has claimed that a representative of the United States (US) Embassy once asked him about the party's proposed candidate for prime minister during a meeting at the US Embassy in Malaysia. Hadi said the question was raised after two senior Pas leaders, Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and Datuk Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, had earlier met the US ambassador. "He asked, 'Who does Pas propose as prime minister?'

items.title: How haze from Indonesian fires impacts Southeast Asia
items.summary: JAKARTA: Thick smog has blanketed parts of Indonesia as the vast archipelago for weeks battles to contain fires that have burned large swathes of Borneo and Sumatra. WHAT CAUSES THE FIRES? "El Nino does not ignite fires.

items.title: Sabah losing experienced medical staff after training, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah is losing experienced medical personnel as trained staff leave the state after completing their training, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad. Dzulkefly said only 12 medical specialists reported for duty in Sabah last year, while 57 transferred out of the state. At present, Sabah has 2,546 doctors, 549 specialists and 10,164 nurses serving in the state.

items.title: Melaka to study proposal to set basic salary at RM2,500-RM2,800, says CM
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 5 — The Melaka government will study a proposal to make the state one of the earliest in Malaysia to set a basic salary of between RM2,500 and RM2,800 before submitting its recommendation to the Federal Government. Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said the proposal would be assessed from all angles before being submitted to the Federal Government. He said the state government would also create opportunities for women who had left their careers due to various factors, particularly through new projects being developed in the state.

items.title: Smart deployment to Nepal gives hope to families
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The deployment of Malaysia's Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) to Nepal has renewed hope among families awaiting news of their missing loved ones. Jamaliah Tengku Ismail, 67, said she had not given up hope of finding her husband, Muhamad Nasir Abdul Talib, 68. Earlier, the eleven-member Smart team departed for Nepal to join the humanitarian mission.

items.title: Malaysia may see 230 million tonnes of plastic waste by 2040, with 23 million entering waterways yearly, says ministry
items.summary: Deputy secretary-general (Environmental Sustainability) Datuk Nor Yahati Awang pointed out that approximately 23 million tonnes of this plastic waste are discharged into waterways annually, representing a significant threat to marine ecosystems. In response, she said NRES has formulated a range of strategies and initiatives to enhance marine waste management nationwide, including the development of a uniform monitoring framework through coastal clean-up programmes. “These efforts include beach clean-ups, systematic data collection, and monitoring.

items.title: Reintroduce GST if it is more effective than SST, says DAP MP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A government backbencher believes that it is better for the government to reintroduce the Goods and Services Tax (GST) if it is more effective than the Sales and Services Tax (SST). Kepong member of Parliament Lim Lip Eng made the suggestion after taking into account views that the SST should be combined with the GST to ensure a more effective taxation system. Lim, who is also the Kuala Lumpur DAP secretary, said the government should not create a complicated hybrid tax system merely to avoid using the GST label.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms and heavy rain in eight states until 6pm
items.summary: MetMalaysia said in a statement that the weather conditions were expected in Kedah, Penang, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Sarawak and Sabah. The affected areas are Bandar Baharu and Kulim in Kedah, Seberang Perai Selatan, Seberang Perai Tengah and Seberang Perai Utara (Penang), and Kinta, Kampar, Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang and Kuala Kangsar (Perak). The warning also covers Gua Musang, Kuala Krai and Jeli (Kelantan), Besut (Terengganu) and Cameron Highlands (Pahang).

items.title: Kafe Secangkir closes its doors after owner's tragic death
items.summary: KUANTAN: Kafe Secangkir in Sungai Karang Darat here, which was run by the late Nur Atiqah Sofiya Mohd Kazwan, closed its doors yesterday and will be handed over to a new tenant. Her brother, Muhammad Hafiz Rifqi, 33, said the decision on the new tenant would be up to the premises' owner. Commenting on the unexpected turnout, particularly on Kafe Secangkir's final day yesterday, Hafiz expressed his appreciation for the support shown by customers.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain expected in eight states until 6pm
items.summary: MetMalaysia said in a statement that the weather conditions were expected in Kedah, Penang, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Sarawak and Sabah. The affected areas are Bandar Baharu and Kulim in Kedah, Seberang Perai Selatan, Seberang Perai Tengah and Seberang Perai Utara (Penang), and Kinta, Kampar, Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang and Kuala Kangsar (Perak). The warning also covers Gua Musang, Kuala Krai and Jeli (Kelantan), Besut (Terengganu) and Cameron Highlands (Pahang).

items.title: Abdul Karim: Kuching gears up for Malaysia Day celebration expected to draw 5,000
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 5 — Approximately 5,000 people are expected to gather at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) for the Malaysia Day celebration on September 16. He added that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg are also expected to attend the official ceremony, scheduled to begin at 8.15 pm. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, who is this year’s Malaysia Day celebration co-chairman, will attend the meeting online.

items.title: Six areas in Sarawak record very unhealthy air quality as of 1pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Six areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy air quality, with Serian registering the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 287 as of 1pm today. No areas recorded hazardous air quality. She said 25 other areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality, while 26 recorded moderate readings and 11 recorded good air quality.

items.title: Melaka eyes RM2,500 basic salary for workers
items.summary: MELAKA: The Melaka government will study a proposal to make the state one of the earliest in Malaysia to set a basic salary of between RM2,500 and RM2,800 before submitting its recommendation to the Federal Government. Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said the proposal would be assessed from all angles before being submitted to the Federal Government. He said the state government would also create opportunities for women who had left their careers due to various factors, particularly through new projects being developed in the state.

items.title: Four held over cable thefts in Kampar and Kuala Kangsar
items.summary: IPOH: Police detained four local men early yesterday morning in connection with two separate cable theft cases in Kampar and Kuala Kangsar. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the first arrest in Kampar was made at about 4.30am when a Malim Nawar Police Station patrol team spotted two men, aged 42 and 46, acting suspiciously at the Muniswarar Temple in Bata Malim Nawar. He said the inspection resulted in the seizure of two cable cutters and five rolls of cable, which Telekom Malaysia (TM) technicians later confirmed belonged to the company.

items.title: First United Sikhs Malaysia team arrives in Nepal to aid flood victims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The first batch of United Sikhs Malaysia volunteers has arrived in Kathmandu on a humanitarian mission to assist families affected by the Nepal floods and support efforts to locate missing Malaysians. United Sikhs Malaysia legal director Raspreet Kaur told the New Straits Times that the team's immediate priority was to reach vulnerable families, particularly those in underserved and hard-to-access areas. Raspreet said Team A would assess access routes and ground conditions before entering the affected areas, while Teams B and C would remain on standby depending on needs on the ground.

items.title: Zahid's absence at Pas Muktamar does not mean Umno will go solo in Melaka polls
items.summary: KOTA BARU: A senior Pas leader said Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's absence from the Pas Muktamar yesterday did not mean Umno intended to go solo in the Melaka election. Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the Umno president, who is also deputy prime minister, was unable to attend due to certain circumstances. Zahid was unable to attend the opening ceremony of the Pas Muktamar yesterday due to unavoidable circumstances.

items.title: Haze affects tourist arrivals and upcoming events in Sarawak, says state minister
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 5 — Sarawak has seen a slight drop in tourist arrivals amid the current haze, said State Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah. He said the decline was expected to continue until the haze situation improved. Abdul Karim said tourists planning to visit Sarawak might change their travel plans due to the haze.

items.title: Fadhlina recounts ordeal of child abuse by caregiver, loss of another to SIDS
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said her personal experiences of child abuse and loss had strengthened her commitment to improving caregiver support for working mothers. Fadhlina said her second child was abused by a caregiver who hit the child on the legs while she was working as a lawyer with a demanding schedule. Fadhlina, who has six children, said three of them had been placed under the care of caregivers, adding that finding suitable childcare was a major challenge for working mothers.

items.title: 27 illegal snares destroyed in Selangor, Perak wildlife operation
items.summary: Perhilitan director-general Datuk Abdul Kadir Abu Hashim said the 27 snares comprised spring traps, wire loop snares and nylon loop snares. "The type and size of snares used generally depend on the species of wildlife being targeted. "Spring traps are commonly used to target wild boar, while wire and nylon loop snares can be used to target larger or smaller wildlife, depending on the diameter of the wire or rope and the size of the spring mechanism used," he said in a statement today.

items.title: MACC detains company owner for allegedly soliciting RM30,000 to secure defence‑sector financing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Kuala Lumpur has arrested an owner of a consulting, management and business company on suspicion of soliciting and accepting bribes of about RM30,000 in return for obtaining grants and loans under the Bumiputera entrepreneur financial financing scheme for two companies related to armaments and defence. According to sources, the woman, in her 60s, was arrested at about 6.45pm on Thursday around Kuala Lumpur. Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohamad Zakkuan Talib when contacted confirmed the arrest and the case is being investigated under Section 16(a) (A) of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: 11 detained to assist probe into group attack in Ipoh
items.summary: Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the 26-year-old victim was approached by five men travelling in two cars at about 10.30am, who then chased and assaulted him. Mohd Alwi said members of the public later came to the victim's aid before taking him to hospital for treatment. Mohd Alwi said all those arrested, aged between 22 and 41, had previous criminal records involving drug offences and violent crimes.

items.title: Serian tops very unhealthy API readings as six Sarawak areas exceed 200
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — A total of six areas in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at very unhealthy levels as of 1pm today with Serian recording the highest reading of 287. Deputy Director-General (Development) of the Department of Environment (DOE) Azuri Azizah Saedon said five other areas in the state that recorded very unhealthy readings were Kuching (267), Sri Aman (251), Samarahan (242), Samalaju (202) and Bintulu (201). She said 25 areas recorded API readings at unhealthy levels involving Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Johor, Pahang, Sabah, Labuan, Sarawak and Selangor, in addition to 26 areas recording moderate air quality status and 11 areas at good levels.

items.title: From janitor to senior lecturer: UM academic turns experience into PhD research
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: From collecting rubbish as a janitor to becoming a senior lecturer at Universiti Malaya, Dr Nurul Asmaa Akmal Md Din has turned years of hard work into an academic career. Nurul Asmaa, 30, drew on her experience in waste management for her doctoral research. She said the job proved valuable rather than a setback, with her experience in waste management later forming the basis of her PhD research.

items.title: Pas-Umno ummah unity must move beyond resolutions, says Tuan Ibrahim
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The ummah unity between Pas and Umno, which was unanimously endorsed at the Islamist party's muktamar, must be translated into action. Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said support for the unity would usually be tested when negotiations on seat allocations for the general election begin. "The muktamar has unanimously approved the strengthening of ummah unity, particularly with many people talking about unity or cooperation between Pas and Umno.

items.title: In Nepal for eight days, Malaysian wife presses on with search for missing special‑operations firefighter
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Hani Othman, who has been in Nepal for eight days to follow the developments in the search for her missing Special Airborne Fire and Rescue Team (PASKUB) officer husband, today joined a mission to distribute humanitarian aid to disaster victims in the country, while hoping to find any clues as to her husband. Hani, who is currently on her way from Nuwakot to Betrawati with the local non-governmental organisations (NGO) Samundra Nepal NGO and Himalayan Leaders, said that the area they are heading to is not the last location where her husband’s vehicle was detected, but she still hopes that the journey will yield clues. “The area of my husband’s last point is further up.

items.title: Haze-linked health problems on the rise, asthma cases jump eightfold
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Asthma, bronchitis, acute respiratory tract infections (URTI) and conjunctivitis are among the health problems reported to have increased amid the haze currently blanketing the country. Public health medicine specialist Datuk Dr Zainal Ariffin Omar said the increase was linked to inflammation of the respiratory tract caused by haze. "Conjunctivitis can also occur as haze particles directly irritate the eyes," he said.

items.title: Malaysia sends families’ DNA samples to Nepal to help identify 55 missing Malaysians, says Tok Mat
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 5 — All DNA samples from the next-of-kin of 55 Malaysians still unaccounted for following floods and landslides in Nepal have been obtained, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. He said the samples would be sent to Nepal for the authorities there to conduct DNA matching, a process expected to take some time given the large number of victims involved. Mohamad said Malaysia was also prepared to send experts from the Department of Chemistry to assist the Nepalese authorities with the DNA matching process, if required.

items.title: Chew Jetty heritage site unaffected by blaze, Penang govt to help owners of five destroyed premises, says CM
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 5 — The historic Chew Jetty here was unaffected by a fire that broke out about 20 metres away and destroyed five business premises early this morning, said Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow. He said the state government was ready to provide assistance to the owners of the five business premises, including support for rebuilding efforts. Chow said the Penang Fire and Rescue Department, assisted by the Volunteer Fire Brigade, had brought the fire under control, while efforts to remove the timber stacks continued after traces of the fire were detected in the wooden structures.

items.title: ‘If Langkawi too small’: Defence minister says LIMA may need alternative venue
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 5 — The proposal to explore an alternative venue for the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA) in the future is aimed at keeping the event competitive amid growing competition among defence exhibitions in the region. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said continuous improvements to LIMA, particularly in terms of venue size and facilities, were necessary, especially as more neighbouring countries were also organising similar exhibitions. Mohamed Khaled said the government should consider developments in the defence exhibition industry in neighbouring countries, which now offer more extensive facilities and exhibition space.

items.title: Government ready to declare emergency if API exceeds 400, says Arthur Kurup
items.summary: KUALA BERANG, Sept 5 — The government is ready to propose declaring an emergency for any area that records an Air Pollution Index (API) reading of more than 400, in line with the standard operating procedure for haze management in the country. Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the measure could be considered if the API reading was at a very dangerous level, as happened in Serian, Sarawak which recorded a reading of more than 500, leading to the declaration of an emergency. Arthur said so far only three of the 68 API monitoring stations nationwide had recorded very unhealthy readings, namely in Kuching, Samarahan and Sri Aman in Sarawak, while Serian recorded readings at a dangerous level.

items.title: ‘Not just Kota Kinabalu’: MOH targets Sandakan, Tawau clusters in Sabah specialist expansion
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 5 — The Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH) will begin placing resident specialists in several hospitals in Sabah such as Kota Marudu and Beaufort as a measure to overcome the shortage of specialists in the state. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the effort also complements the ministry’s initiative to move specialist rotation to rural areas in Sabah. Dr Dzulkefly said MOH has also aggressively expanded the Hospital Services Outsourcing Programme initiative to the private sector to address congestion in public hospital lobbies and wards.

items.title: Serian town unusually quiet amid thick haze and emergency declaration
items.summary: SERIAN, Sept 5 — The usually vibrant streets of Serian town, typically bustling with weekend crowds, appeared unusually quiet today, amidst the ongoing haze and the declaration of an emergency in the area. A Bernama check around the town found that health concerns had disrupted daily activities. However, the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal showed a downward trend from the hazardous levels above 500 recorded the day before.

items.title: Thai DPM Sihasak to undertake two‑day working visit to Malaysia from Sept 6
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Thailand’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Sihasak Phuangketkeow, is scheduled to pay a two-day working visit to Malaysia from Sunday to September 7, according to the PR Thai Government. In its Facebook post on Friday, it noted that the visit would follow up on and advance the issues discussed by the leaders of the two countries during the Thai Prime Minister’s official visit to Malaysia on July 9 to 10. The delegation is scheduled to meet Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan to discuss border security and joint development of border areas.

items.title: Zambry: Malaysia Higher Education Plan 2026-2035 aims to shape students with strong values alongside academic excellence
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 5 — The Malaysia Higher Education Plan (RPTM) 2026–2035 is focused on developing students who are not only academically competent but also grounded in strong values and good character. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the goal of education is not merely to produce knowledgeable and skilled graduates, but to shape better individuals who are capable of navigating a changing world and the demands of the job market. “The purpose of education is to make us better people.

items.title: Workplaces in Serian may operate during haze emergency with health precautions, says SDMC
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 5 — Government, private offices and other workplaces affected by the haze emergency in Serian, including industries, plantations, construction sites and quarries may continue their operations but must take health precautionary measures. Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas, who is also state Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman, said the committee is closely monitoring the haze situation across Sarawak, particularly the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading in Serian. “SDMC is currently monitoring the API level in Serian within these three days in anticipation for any fluctuation of the API level, should it increase to a level above 500.

items.title: Nadma sends 11‑member SMART team to Nepal for flood and landslide SAR
items.summary: SUBANG, Sept 5 — Eleven personnel and officers from the Special Malaysian Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) departed for Nepal this morning to assist search and rescue (SAR) operations in areas affected by floods and landslides. National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said the team is led by commander Abdul Manaf Che Isa, with the mission expected to last 10 days. Eleven members of the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) depart for Nepal from Subang Air Base September 5, 2026.

items.title: Air Kelantan: Pipe leak cuts water supply in Machang, Pasir Puteh and Kota Bharu Selatan, affecting 34,000 accounts
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 5 — Production capacity at the Merbau Chondong Water Treatment Plant (WTP) in Machang has dropped by almost half following a leak in a 1,000-millimetre Glass-Fibre Reinforced Plastic (GRP) raw water pipe, said Air Kelantan Sdn Bhd (AKSB). In a statement today, AKSB said the incident had disrupted water supply in three districts, namely Machang, parts of Pasir Puteh and Kota Bharu Selatan, affecting almost 34,000 consumer accounts. AKSB is also mobilising water tankers to assist affected consumers, while water operators from other states have also agreed to send tankers to the affected areas,” AKSB said.

items.title: PM to deliver closing address and present Agro Awards at MAHA 2026 tomorrow
items.summary: SERDANG, Sept 5 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to officiate the closing ceremony of the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agro-Tourism Exhibition (MAHA 2026) at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park (MAEPS), here tomorrow. Based on the programme, Anwar is scheduled to arrive at 10.30 am before delivering the Closing Address at Hall D2 and performing the Closing Gimmick of MAHA 2026. Also scheduled to be present are the two Deputy Prime Ministers and Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.

items.title: MOH: Malaysia to lead 17th Asean Health Ministers Meeting in Kuala Lumpur from Sept 7-11
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Malaysia will chair the 17th Asean Health Ministers Meeting (AHMM), which begins September 7 in the capital, the Ministry of Health (MOH) announced. Organised by the MOH, the conference reflects the ministry’s pivotal role as a leader in regional health diplomacy, tasked with coordinating policy directions, digital health innovation and health crisis preparedness at the Asean level. Held biennially, the AHMM is the primary platform for Asean Health Ministers to discuss regional health issues and strengthen collaboration and coordination across the health sector.

items.title: Public briefing on Sarawak electoral boundary review set for Sept 8 in Kuching
items.summary: ROSE president Geoffrey Tang said the session would feature EC commissioner Mohd Faisal Syam Abdul Hazis, who would be accompanied by EC Sarawak director Abang Noraffian Abang Ibrahim. “Electoral boundary review is an important process that has a direct impact on how people are represented in the electoral system,” he said in a statement. he said.

items.title: Understand and follow guidelines before flying Jalur Gemilang, including AI‑generated images, says national unity minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Malaysians are urged to exercise greater care and always refer to the proper guidelines when installing and displaying the Jalur Gemilang. National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said the Jalur Gemilang was a symbol of national sovereignty, dignity and unity that all Malaysians, regardless of race, religion or political affiliation, must respect. Aaron said the National Unity Ministry, through the Kawasan Rukun Tetangga (KRT) and Rukun Negara Secretariat, would step up efforts to raise public awareness of the correct procedures for installing and displaying the Jalur Gemilang.

items.title: Perak exco hopes Budget 2027 will prioritise welfare of older rural residents
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 5 — The Perak state government hopes Budget 2027 will give special attention to the welfare of senior citizens in rural areas, covering housing, basic amenities, mobility as well as digital access. State Rural Development, Plantation, Agriculture and Food Industry Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Zolkafly Harun said the attention was important with the increasing elderly population in the state, as well as the migration of young people to urban areas, which resulted in some senior citizens in rural areas, especially those living alone, to face limited access to support facilities. He also drew attention to housing, stressing that serious attention was needed as there were still low-income (B40) groups in rural areas living in houses that were too dilapidated and no longer economically viable to repair.
